OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized
            to E.164 form; a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true on create, allows registering this owner even if another
            owner already has the same last name and postal address (compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) because they share a household.
            Otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict. Request-only; not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0

The restructure is complete and verified.

## What I did

**One behavior-preserving refactor** in `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`: extracted `findHousemates(Owner)` out of `isHouseholdInUse(Owner)`.

- `findHousemates` returns the `List<Owner>` of existing owners in the same household (same normalized last name + address), using the exact matching logic that was previously inlined in the boolean check.
- `isHouseholdInUse` now delegates: `return !findHousemates(owner).isEmpty();`

## Why this is the right preparation

The current `addOwner` already handles the `sharesHousehold` flag for the *conflict* decision (skipping the 409 when true). The upcoming change adds the missing half: when an owner joins an existing household, it must **copy that household's `householdId`**, and otherwise **mint a new one**. That needs the *actual* matching owners in hand — but today the only household query, `isHouseholdInUse`, throws that information away by collapsing to a boolean.

`findHousemates` is exactly the seam the change needs:
- It gives `addOwner` the housemate list to read a shared `householdId` from (`assignHouseholdId`), and an empty list is the signal to `generateHouseholdId`.
- It slots into the controller's established idiom of small private helpers (`generateCustomerCode`, `normalizeTelephone`, `normalizeHouseholdField`, …), so the new `assignHouseholdId` / `generateHouseholdId` helpers will read as natural neighbours rather than swelling `addOwner` inline.
- `findHousemates` is named exactly as the change would want it, so the change lands as small additions, not a rewrite of the household logic.

I deliberately did **not** touch the `Owner` entity (adding a `householdId` field/column), the OpenAPI response schema, or `addOwner`'s flow — those are the change itself, not preparation.

## Verification

- Baseline (before): full suite compiles; the only test, `AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId`, fails with an NPE at line 21 because `householdId` isn't in the response yet — it's the pre-written acceptance spec for the *upcoming* change.
- After my refactor: **identical state** — compiles cleanly, app boots, same single test fails at the same line for the same unimplemented-`householdId` reason. No behavior changed, no new failures, nothing that was green went red.

That remaining red test is the change's acceptance criterion, which I was explicitly instructed not to implement yet.
